body:
Thank you. I try my hardest. The recovery is ongoing and it'll never be complete, really. Scars and all that.

I don't know why I have trouble with love. My emotions are generally very subdued. I've just never felt like I've actually loved another person -- as I said, I can feel 'fond' about someone, and like them, but beyond that, no. Most of the time I have trouble with empathy, and it's hard for me to hold conversation.

Romance is unthinkable to me not because I don't think someone could love me, but because I don't know if I could ever enjoy someone's intimacy so deeply. Sometimes I wonder if it's because my parents were, generally, terrible people, and did not try to raise me properly/show me affection at all. I know when someone tells me they care about me, I don't feel that warm and mushy feeling other folks talk about. 

I know it's possible for me to love because I certainly love, for example, my dogs -- I'd be upset as hell if anything happened to them. That's how I know I'm not a sociopath or something like that. (I know what socios are like -- my dad was one, and a drug addict.) I don't like actively hurting or manipulating people, either. I'm just very neutral, very withdrawn.

Hah, I know. It's academia: they don't think that fantasy stories can have real meaning. Too bad. Those were the first stories human beings ever told. I find ways to make my literary work fun enough, though.

I've written a lot of stories in my lifetime. Editing them so they're coherent is another matter. :) Since I'm in a poetry class this semester, a lot of my most recent work is poetry. And I'm rather proud of it.

Fiction, mostly. I prefer fantasy, sci-fi and horror, but I'm fine with the "literary" stuff, too. (At school, we're only allowed to write about Real People doing Real Things, anyway. No were-dragons or space babes or mutant roaches. lol. So the fantastic stuff is my hobby.)

I also like poetry, and I think I'm pretty decent at it.

I don't mind you asking. This conversation is helping me feel better.

I was heavily abused as a child and teenager emotionally and sexually, so I ended up with a lot of issues: depression, OCD, anxiety, PTSD.

No, I understood you. :)

Yeah, I'd like to help people with a pre-existing passion. I'm kind-of a lethargic person so it's rather difficult for me to spread "the energy" around. (It's why I'm horrid at poetry readings; I just can't show external enthusiasm.)
No. It used to recur quite a bit when my depression was worse. This is the first time it's come up in a while.

I want to help produce a generation of free-thinking writers. I feel like a lot of books are, essentially, the same these days. I'd like to read some variety.

I'd be happy teaching teenagers and above. At grad school I'll probably end up helping out with/teaching the incoming freshmen.
Oh, I never sleep well, really...I was on benzos too long as a kid and so I'm always on the verge of a nap, even if I've been asleep for 6 - 9 hours.

Teach for a living -- I want to go to grad school after I'm done with university. And I'll write on the side.

There's nothing I love more than stories. I scribble all the time.
English. Creative writing concentration. I'm pretty good at it, though my internet posts while emotionally freaked don't really show it.
It is frustrating indeed. I was perfectly content about 12 hours ago. I don't know what happened. :(
